figures.caption: Figure 1: The applicability criterion as a pre-flight decision rule. Both checks are run before any classifier is trained: the augmented Dickey–Fuller test screens stationarity, and a saturated per-channel power baseline screens for power-discrimination. Only tasks that pass both are in the descriptor’s domain of validity.

Table 1: The applicability criterion applied to all six paradigms. Each prediction follows from the two preconditions of Figure 1 (stationarity and coupling-borne class information) before the experiment; the observed column reports the measured outcome. Predictions and observations agree in every row.

Table 2: EEG results across two paradigms, two protocols. Bootstrap 95% CIs from nboot=1000 resamples (test-epoch level for within-subject; subject-level for LOSO mean). Last column = P (D(τ)>PSD) under bootstrap.

Table 4: Learned heads on top of D(τ) embeddings. Bold = best non-deep result for that paradigm. References at the bottom of each section are class-aware (BCI: CSP+LDA, sleep: published deep methods).

Table 5: Symmetric vs asymmetric D(τ) across five benchmarks (NC = nearest-centroid; LDA / MLP = learned heads). Bold per row group marks the best variant for each classifier column. Asymmetric helps NC only on the two single-subject oscillatory paradigms (Sleep, BCI subj 1); LOSO and audio benchmarks see asymmetric phase wash out. Learned heads prefer the symmetric default everywhere.

Table 8: Sleep-EDF 20-subject LOSO: the training-free D(τ) descriptor against a classical trainingfree baseline (PSD) and a tuned modern self-supervised representation (TS2Vec [13]), under the identical protocol and classifier heads. “Repr. cost” is the single-CPU wall-clock to turn raw epochs into the embedding; D(τ) and PSD require no training. All three are statistically tied on accuracy; D(τ) matches the tuned learned representation at ∼25× lower cost. TS2Vec is shown both untuned (unnormalized input) and tuned (z-scored input, given D(τ)’s own multi-band front-end).
Figure 2: τmax ×K ablation on Sleep-EDF (5-class). MLP is highly robust across the grid; NC has a sharp optimum at low-K, long-τmax.

Table 10: Channel-dropout robustness on BCI-IV-2a (4-class, 9-subj mean ± SD). Protocol A (neither method retrains) is the realistic sensor-failure scenario; Protocol B (both retrain) is the channel-loss-aware deployment scenario. Under Protocol A, D(τ)+MLP is dramatically more robust: CSP+LDA’s spatial filters collapse to chance at just 10% drop, while D(τ)+MLP degrades smoothly. Under Protocol B (both adaptive), CSP+LDA retains its ∼14 pp accuracy lead.
